record.paper_title: Open problems posed at the eighth international conference on fuzzy set theory and applications
record.original_question: A fuzzy implication is a function I: [0, 1]^2 -> [0, 1] that is non-increasing in its first component, non-decreasing in its second component, satisfies I(1, 0) = 0, and satisfies I(0, x) = I(x, 1) = 1 for every x in [0, 1]. A t-norm T is an associative, commutative, non-decreasing operation on [0, 1] with neutral element 1. For a given continuous t-norm T, characterize all fuzzy implications I satisfying the law of importation I(x, I(y, z)) = I(T(x, y), z) for all x, y, z in [0, 1]. Since commutativity of T makes this law imply the exchange principle I(x, I(y, z)) = I(y, I(x, z)), does the exchange principle conversely imply the existence of a t-norm T for which the law of importation holds? If so, is T unique; if not, give an example and characterize the fuzzy implications for which the converse is true.

evidence.quote: A function I : [0, 1]^2 -> [0, 1] is called a (fuzzy) implication if it is non-increasing in its first component, non-decreasing in its second component and satisfies I(1, 0) = 0.
For a given (continuous) t-norm T, characterize all fuzzy implications which satisfy the law of importation with respect to T.
Does the exchange principle imply that there exists a t-norm such that the law of importation holds? If yes, is the t-norm uniquely determined?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A fuzzy implication is a function I:[0,1]^2 → [0,1] that is non-increasing in its first argument, non-decreasing in its second argument, and satisfies I(1,0)=0 together with I(0,x)=I(x,1)=1 for every x∈[0,1]. A t-norm is a binary operation T:[0,1]^2 → [0,1] that is associative, commutative, non-decreasing in each argument, and has 1 as neutral element. Given a t-norm T, a fuzzy implication I is said to satisfy the law of importation with respect to T (denoted LI(T)) if
   I(x, I(y, z)) = I(T(x,y), z) for all x,y,z ∈ [0,1].
A fuzzy implication I satisfies the exchange principle (EP) if
   I(x, I(y, z)) = I(y, I(x, z)) for all x,y,z ∈ [0,1].

Address the following:

(a) For an arbitrary (in particular, continuous) t-norm T, give a complete characterization of all fuzzy implications I that satisfy LI(T).

(b) Since the commutativity of T implies that LI(T) entails EP, investigate the converse: does every fuzzy implication I satisfying the exchange principle satisfy LI(T) for some t-norm T? If so, is such a T uniquely determined by I? If not, exhibit a counterexample and characterize precisely the class of fuzzy implications for which the converse implication does hold (and for which uniqueness of T holds).
artifact.status_search_result: Substantial progress has been made on both parts. For (a), characterizations of fuzzy implications satisfying LI(T) have been obtained for the minimum t-norm, continuous Archimedean t-norms, ordinal sums thereof, and in particular for fuzzy implications with continuous natural negation under any continuous t-norm T (Massanet–Torrens, IEEE TFS 2016, and follow-up work through 2021). For (b), it has been shown that LI is strictly stronger than EP and that EP does not in general imply the existence of a t-norm T with LI(T); partial classes for which the converse holds have been identified. A fully general characterization remains incomplete, so the overall problem is partially solved.

status_evidence.title: Characterization of Fuzzy Implication Functions With a Continuous Natural Negation Satisfying the Law of Importation With a Fixed t-Norm
status_evidence.snippet: Given a fixed t-norm T, all fuzzy implication functions with continuous natural negation that satisfy the law of importation with this t-norm T are characterized.
status_evidence.claim: Part (a) is solved for continuous t-norms under the restriction of continuous natural negation.

status_evidence.title: The law of importation versus the exchange principle on fuzzy implications
status_evidence.snippet: The law of importation is stronger than the exchange principle.
status_evidence.claim: LI strictly implies EP; the converse direction (b) is the subject of active study.

status_evidence.title: Characterization of a class of fuzzy implication solutions to the law of importation
status_evidence.snippet: Characterization of a class of fuzzy implication solutions to the law of importation.
status_evidence.claim: Further classes of solutions have been characterized, but no complete general characterization exists.
